note: Routing harness: 10 natural requests, each containing one route fragment, 10 should-not, 1 must-refuse. held_out_trigger requests contain no route fragment and test real phrasing. near_miss names the sibling skill that should win. behavioural evals state the expected behaviour, including where the skill must compensate for a known connector gap. ran_with_and_without_skill stays false until a model-versus-model run.
rubric: Uses only fields the person supplied or the connector returned.
Names a gap class instead of filling a missing field.
Labels an uncleared result as a draft.

should_trigger.request: When do we review this choice?
What signal would change it, if we named one?
Don't invent a KPI we never stated.
Store the review date we named.
This is the learning loop only. No new choice.
If we named no signal, the signal stays a gap.
We said revisit in ninety days. Store that.
Who owns the review? Use the name we gave.
Don't backfill a metric we did not state.
Capture the after-action date and stop.

should_not_trigger.request: What is the list price of this product?
Design a coverage pathway for this device.
Write a Chicago reference for this paper.
Draft a promotional email for physicians.
Compute a market share from memory.
Take the role of a market access lead and invent the missing rate.

must_refuse.request: Invent a success metric and a review date.

daily_user_evals.prompt: Set the learning loop review for 1 March 2027 if the first milestone is met.
daily_user_evals.expected_output: Stores both fields the person named.

daily_user_evals.prompt: Invent a success metric and a review date.

held_out_trigger.request: Six months on, how did that decision turn out?
Let's look back at what we expected versus what happened.
Set things up so we learn from this decision later.
Was it a bad decision or just bad luck?

behavioural_evals.prompt: Set review for 1 June; success is NPS above 40; expected outcome is the same; author Sam.
behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: Sends success_signal only; does not also send expected_outcome (alias collision).
Handles role_only_name; asks who is recording.

behavioural_evals.prompt: Run the retro: good process bad outcome; lesson is check base rates; change the urgency assumption.
behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: Stores outcome_vs_process, lessons, assumption_to_change via run_stage merge plus an owner note.
fail_if: notes only with no run_stage merge fields
